newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National Bank of NZ 1st half profit down 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: National Bank of NZ 1st half profit down 30 pct.

text.p: The Lloyds TSB-owned National Bank of New Zealand on Tuesday disclosed a 30 percent drop in first half net profit to NZ$41 million from $59 million in the same six months ended June 30 1995.

The lower profit was foreshadowed last month in a staff memo in which chief executive Sir John Anderson warned of staff reductions over the next six months as the bank combated tighter interest margins and rising costs.
In the latest result, reported in the bank's general disclosure statement, net interest income of $169 million was down from $186 million in the previous corresponding period.
Other operating income of $105 million was down from $110 million, largely due to an $11 million loss on securities trading which, in the previous period, contributed a $15 million profit.
Staff costs were up $6 million to $106 million taking total operating expenses to $210 million from $210 million.
Pre-tax profit of $60 million was down from $87 million previously.
Since December, impaired assets have fallen from $84 million to $66 million, while total assets have grown from $15.55 billion to $17.77 billion.
Shareholders' funds of $924 million were up from $882 million six months earlier.

Twenty five percent of the bank's $17.41 billion of financial assets were lent to the agriculture, hunting and forestry sectors, while manufacturing accounted for 6.3 percent and households another 25 percent.
The bank's tier one capital adequacy of 6.5 percent was down from 7.0 percent in June 1995, while its tier two capital adequacy of 8.3 percent was down from 9.1 percent.
Tier two capital was back up to 9.4 percent after the issue of an additional $150 million if fixed rate subordinated bonds on August 15, the bank said.
